findings.title: Unconditional or True in supervisor_tools exception handler masks errors and misroutes failures
findings.impact: Any exception raised during parallel research task execution in supervisor_tools (such as network errors, API rate limits, authentication failures, or bugs) will be caught and unconditionally treated as a token limit exceeded event due to or True. This prematurely terminates the research phase and returns partial notes instead of propagating or handling the error correctly.
findings.preconditions: An exception e is raised during asyncio.gather(*research_tasks) in supervisor_tools.
findings.explanation: The boolean expression is_token_limit_exceeded(e, configurable.research_model) or True always evaluates to True. Consequently, even when is_token_limit_exceeded returns false, the code enters the if block, masking the original exception and ending the research process.
findings.suggestion: Remove or True from the conditional check so that non-token-limit exceptions are not incorrectly caught and swallowed as token limit errors.

findings.title: Unconditional Exception Handling Force-Termination in Supervisor Tools
findings.impact: Any exception occurring during parallel research execution is unconditionally caught and forces the supervisor to abruptly terminate the research phase, leading to denial of service or premature termination of research tasks.
findings.preconditions: An exception is raised during parallel research execution within the try-except block.
findings.explanation: Line 334 evaluates `if is_token_limit_exceeded(e, configurable.research_model) or True:`, which always resolves to true regardless of the exception type, bypassing intended token limit checks and causing immediate workflow termination.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `or True` condition so that only actual token limit exceptions trigger the specific termination path, or handle other exceptions appropriately.
